item.title: BGMEA: RMG unrest costs 317 factories $428m in 18 days
item.description:
Bangladesh’s readymade garment (RMG) sector has suffered severe setbacks due to ongoing unrest, with 317 surveyed factories reporting $428 million in production losses and $254 million worth of confirmed orders shifted to other countries over an 18-day period from November 1 to November 18.
The figures emerged from an urgent four-day survey conducted by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) among member factories to assess the impact of recent disruptions, according to a press release issued on Sunday and signed by BGMEA secretary general Maj Gen Md Shahedul Islam (retd).
The 317 factories that responded to the survey were forced to halt production anywhere from one day to a maximum of 16 days between November 1 and November 18 due to instability, resulting in $428 million in direct production loss in FOB value.
Beyond the $428 million direct loss, most orders face severe risk due to missed delivery timelines, forcing factories to contend with costly air shipments, steep price discounts, and outright order cancellations to retain business.
Eroded buyer confidence led international buyers to shift 59 million pieces of garments—valued at $254 million—from confirmed orders to rival destinations, according to participating factories.
BGMEA noted that the survey findings reflect only a partial picture of the overall damage, as more than 600 member factories have been affected while only 317 could participate within the brief survey window, and instability in industrial belts has continued beyond November 18.
According to the association, the deeper blow is to the long-term global image, reliability, and future prospects of Bangladesh's apparel industry—a trend already visible in the diversion of orders to competing countries.
Urging a swift resolution in the interest of the national economy and the livelihoods of millions of workers, BGMEA called on all concerned stakeholders to act with maximum responsibility and take effective steps to keep the sector running and overcome the crisis.

item.title: Tk11.67cr gold paste seizure: Three placed on five-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court has placed three people on a five-day remand each after their arrest with 7.5kg of gold paste worth Tk11.67 crore at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
Additional Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Zakir Hossain of the Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court passed the order on Sunday following a petition by the case investigation officer, Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Shafiqul Islam of Airport Police Station.
The remanded accused are Md Yasin Arafat Sourav, 29, Md Zakirul Islam Jewel, 53, and Md Shawon, 39. Sourav is from Munshiganj Sadar upazila, Zakirul from Sudharam upazila in Noakhali, and Shawon from Barura upazila in Comilla.
Earlier, the investigation officer produced the three accused before the court and sought 10 days of remand for interrogation. After hearing both sides, the court granted five days of remand for each of them.
The defence lawyers sought bail and opposed the remand, while the prosecution argued in favour of the remand.
SI Md Saiful Islam of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Prosecution Division confirmed the matter.
According to sources at the Airport Armed Police Battalion (APBn), the three were detained after attempting to flee upon sensing the presence of police.
A subsequent body search of Sourav at the APBn office recovered 15 oval-shaped objects wrapped in orange cloth and concealed around his waist. Tests conducted by a goldsmith and subsequent chemical analysis confirmed that the objects were gold paste.
The seized gold was found to be 24-carat pure and weighed 7.5kg.
During preliminary interrogation, the detainees said Sourav regularly travelled to Saudi Arabia and used innovative methods to smuggle gold into the country. He allegedly worked with Zakirul, Shawon and other associates to distribute the smuggled gold.
Investigators suspect that the three have long been involved in gold smuggling operations centred around the airport and are active members of an organised smuggling syndicate.
In this connection, SI Md Abul Kalam of Airport Police Station filed a case against them under Sections 25B(1)(b) and 25D of the Special Powers Act, 1974.
The remand was sought for a detailed investigation to identify other members of the syndicate involved in the smuggling operation.

item.title: Police uncover fake visa factory in Chittagong, arrest 1
item.description:
Police in a drive unearthed a fake visa making factory in the city's Teribazar area on Sunday and arrested a man with fake visas, visa-making equipment and 17 Bangladeshi passports.
The arrestee was identified as Abdul Mabud, 53, who was allegedly involved in producing fake visas.
Tipped off, a team of police conducted a drive at a room, located on the 5th floor of Badruddin Market in Katapahar area in the morning and unearthed a fake visa production factory, said Zahedul Kabir, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Kotwali Police Station.
They also arrested Mabud along with 17 Bangladeshi passports, fake visas, various equipment for making fake visas. He was wanted in a case filed with Dhaka Airport Police Station on February 5 on charge of fraudulence.
A case was filed with Kotwali Police Station in connection with the incident.

item.title: BGB initiative opens freelancing opportunities for border-area youths
item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has trained 30 educated unemployed youths from border areas in graphic design and freelancing to help create technology-based employment opportunities.
One of the trainees has already started earning through local assignments and online platforms after completing the training.
The participants received certificates at a ceremony held at Pakhiguria High School in Thakurgaon on Sunday afternoon. Colonel Mohammad Suroj Mia, sector commander of BGB's Thakurgaon sector, handed over the certificates.
The programme was organised by the Paria Company of BGB's Thakurgaon 50 Battalion. Lieutenant Colonel Zubayer Anwar, commanding officer of the battalion, delivered the welcome address.
Speaking at the event, Colonel Suroj Mia said BGB was working not only to protect the country's borders and sovereignty but also to improve the socioeconomic conditions of border communities.
He said the force was implementing various welfare programmes alongside efforts to prevent smuggling and cross-border crimes, with a focus on employment and self-reliance.
Lieutenant Colonel Zubayer Anwar said 100 participants received basic computer training at Mashkhuria High School in Baliadangi upazila from August 2 to November 19. Based on merit, 30 of them were selected for specialised training in graphic design and freelancing.
Taljila Akhter, who secured first place in the post-training examination, said she had already started earning by applying her newly acquired skills.
Another trainee, Robiul Alam of Harinmari village in Baliadangi, said the hands-on training had helped him develop practical skills. He is now looking for employment opportunities.
BGB officials expressed hope that the initiative would help participants become financially self-reliant while contributing to the local economy.

item.title: Satkhira woman farmer leads push for safe agriculture in coastal region
item.description:
Battling salinity and waterlogging caused by climate change, Sarma Rani, a 48-year-old woman farmer in Shyamnagar upazila of Satkhira, is inspiring coastal communities to adopt chemical-free farming.
At her homestead in Mathurapur village under Munshiganj Union, she has transformed 33 decimals of her 66-decimal homestead into a diverse vegetable farm, using organic fertilisers and natural pesticides instead of chemical inputs.
She makes organic fertiliser from kitchen waste, vegetable peels and grass, while preparing natural pesticides using neem leaves and garlic. She also preserves seeds from the crops grown on her land.
Her farming initiative supports her four-member family. With her husband, Bimal Mondal, suffering from illness, she shoulders much of the family's responsibilities. Selling vegetables earns her around Tk7,000 a month, while avoiding chemical fertilisers saves her approximately Tk18,000 annually.
Her commitment to education is another defining aspect of her journey. Forced to discontinue her studies after Class Ten because of financial hardship, she made sure her three daughters received higher education. Her son is now pursuing postgraduate studies at Government Brajalal (BL) College in Khulna.
Sarma Rani has also taken her initiative beyond her homestead. She established the Mathurapur Bakul Women's Agricultural Development Organisation and a local seed bank that preserves around 80 varieties of indigenous seeds. She regularly exchanges seeds with more than 200 women farmers.
Her journey began around 2018 through contact with the Bangladesh Resource Centre for Indigenous Knowledge (BARCIK). After receiving training, she became a trainer herself, conducting around 40 sessions on organic fertiliser and natural pesticide preparation. Nearly 600 women from surrounding villages and unions have received training from her.
The impact is visible among local farmers.
Dipti Rani of Phultala village said she learned organic farming from Sarma Rani and now gets better yields from her papaya trees.
Sarma Rani's homestead preserves seeds of 30 varieties of vegetables, 20 varieties of fruits and 12 indigenous chilli varieties. Her pond contains 24 varieties of native fish.
She now wants to turn safe vegetable cultivation into a social movement across the coastal region.
"Growing chemical-free vegetables on my own is not enough. I want to encourage farmers and families to adopt this practice and produce safe food for their households," she said.
Shyamnagar Upazila Agriculture Officer Oliul Islam praised her initiative, saying the agriculture department would provide technical advice and support to share her experience with other farmers.

item.title: Thousands head to Sundarbans for Rash Festival
item.description:
More than 10,000 Hindu devotees headed for Dublar Char in the Sundarbans on Sunday morning to attend the annual Rash Purnima Puja.
The two-day puja will begin at midnight tonight at Alorkol on Dublar Char, along the Bay of Bengal coast, and conclude Tuesday morning with the traditional holy dip in the sea, according to the Forest Department.
Forest Ranger Md Hamidur Rahman, an officer at Chandpai Station under the Sundarbans East Forest Division said yesterday noon that 6,209 pilgrims had departed for Dublar Char in 294 vessels after obtaining permits from his station.
Another 2,371 pilgrims had left in 111 vessels through Dangmari Station.
Meanwhile, more than 1,500 devotees had also travelled to the island from the Sundarbans West Forest Division, said AZM Tanzir Hossain, divisional forest officer (DFO) of the division.
The West Division also distributed passes, he said.
Freedom Fighter Md Kamal Uddin Ahmed, president of the Dublar Fishermen Group and the Rash Purnima Puja Celebration Committee, said over the phone on Sunday that all preparations for the festival had been completed at Alorkol on Dublar Char.
A temporary temple has been constructed, and idols of Radha and Krishna have been installed for the occasion, he said.
According to the religious calendar, worship, devotional songs and kirtan will be held at the temporary Radha-Krishna temple from midnight tonight.
Thousands of Hindu devotees from different parts of the country, including Satkhira, Khulna, Faridpur, Narail, Dhaka and Bagerhat, are expected to gather at Alorkol.
The pilgrims will take a holy dip in the sea during the first high tide early Tuesday before returning home, Kamal Uddin Ahmed said.
Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) of the Sundarbans East Forest Division, Bagerhat, Md Rezaul Karim Chowdhury, said permits had been issued exclusively to Hindu devotees since yesterday morning.
The Forest Department has designated five routes for safe travel to the festival.
To ensure security and maintain order, forest guards, Coast Guard personnel and Navy members will conduct regular patrols. Forest officials will also maintain strict surveillance to prevent deer hunting and other forms of wildlife poaching during the festival, he added.
According to Forest Department sources, a large fair used to be organised at Alorkol during the Rash Festival for several decades. Pilgrims, visitors and traders from different parts of the country, as well as foreign tourists, would attend the event.
However, the large gatherings, waste generation and noise pollution began posing threats to the biodiversity of the Sundarbans.
Poaching groups also reportedly became active by disguising themselves as pilgrims.
Considering the environmental risks, the fair was discontinued in 2021. Since then, the festival has been restricted to religious rituals and observances.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,352 as nine die in 24 hours
item.description:
Nine more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Sunday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,352.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all nine of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,247, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the nine new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with four deaths.
A total of 1,162 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Sunday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 256,586.
During the same period, 76 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 26,136.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 229,530 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 220,705 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Health groups say COP31 draft falls short on fossil fuels, climate finance
item.description:
Health advocates have criticised the latest draft agreement at the COP31 climate summit, warning that it lacks the concrete commitments needed to protect public health and address the growing threats posed by climate change.
The Global Climate and Health Alliance (GCHA) has called on governments to strengthen climate finance commitments and ensure a just and equitable transition away from fossil fuels as negotiations entered their final stage on Sunday.
Representing more than 300 health professional and civil society organisations and networks worldwide, the alliance raised concerns over the latest draft cover decision, particularly its weakened language on international legal obligations, scientific evidence and fossil fuel dependence.
Jess Beagley, policy lead at GCHA, said the draft acknowledged the links between climate change and health, including the need for climate-resilient health systems and greater protection for children. However, she said this recognition was not backed by concrete commitments.
“The latest text of the cover decision clearly recognises the links between climate change and health impacts, and the need for more climate-resilient health systems, including the importance of protecting children, but there is a chasm between this brief acknowledgement and commitment to real climate action to protect health and lives,” Beagley said in a statement issued on November 22.
The alliance urged developed countries to make stronger climate finance commitments to help developing nations protect vulnerable populations from worsening climate impacts.
“The people of the world need developed countries to make strong commitments to provide climate finance that gives developing countries the resources they need to protect their populations, and to advance global progress towards a just and equitable transition away from fossil fuels,” she said.
Beagley also warned that weakening international cooperation could further endanger public health.
“Without an ongoing commitment to multilateralism people’s health will be placed at increasing risk,” she added.
GCHA expressed particular concern over changes to the draft decision, including the removal of an earlier reference to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) advisory opinion on states' obligations regarding climate change.
The alliance also criticised the draft for failing to explicitly recognise the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) as a source of the best available scientific evidence to guide climate action.
According to Beagley, these omissions risk weakening the scientific and legal foundations of the proposed agreement at a time when stronger international commitments are urgently needed to tackle the climate crisis.
The proposed target to scale up carbon capture and storage was another major concern for the health alliance.
GCHA warned that expanding carbon capture and storage could prolong reliance on fossil fuels, potentially increasing the health risks associated with their continued production and use.
“The latest draft of the cover decision eliminates a previous reference to the ICJ Advisory Opinion on the obligations of States with respect to climate change, fails to directly recognise the IPCC as a source of the best available science to guide climate action, and includes a deeply problematic target to scale up carbon capture and storage which could lead to increased health harms on account of expanded fossil fuel dependence,” Beagley said.
The alliance issued its warning as negotiators awaited a plenary session to consider the proposed agreement, with disagreements continuing over fossil fuels, climate finance and the direction of the global energy transition.
Health advocates are urging governments to ensure that the final outcome goes beyond acknowledging climate-related health risks and includes meaningful commitments to protect lives, support developing countries and accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels.
For the global health community, the success of COP31 will be measured not only by diplomatic agreements but also by whether governments take concrete action to reduce the growing health burden of climate change.

item.title: Milon: Institutions must not become factories producing unemployed graduates
item.description:
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon has said educational institutions must not become factories producing unemployed graduates, stressing the need for stronger links between universities and industries to develop a skilled workforce that meets labour market demands.
He made the remarks at a seminar titled “Industry-Academia Collaboration: Government Policy and the Position of Dhaka University” at the Nawab Nawab Ali Chowdhury Senate Bhaban auditorium of Dhaka University (DU) on Sunday.
The seminar was jointly organised by DU and the University and Industry Alliance.
Milon said university teachers should conduct research at industrial establishments before sending students there for internships. University curricula should be developed based on the findings, while industries must also benefit from collaborating with universities.
He called for joint research and innovation initiatives, saying the government was ready to support the establishment of curriculum advisory boards, innovation hubs and incubators.
Speaking about DU's budget, the minister said there was no shortage of funds for the university or its research activities, but proper utilisation of allocated money must be ensured.
He said the University Grants Commission (UGC) allocates funds while the government provides money to the commission. Of its six members, four are from Dhaka University, he added.
“We have not come here to do politics; we have come here to work,” he said, urging the university to clearly explain its funding requirements, proposed expenditure and expected outcomes.
He also stressed that university research must have practical applications in industry, the economy and employment generation rather than remain limited to academic papers and theses.
Expressing concern over delays in project implementation, he called for greater transparency and accountability in spending allocated funds.
The minister also criticised session jams and lengthy admission procedures, saying students were losing valuable time between completing public examinations, securing university admission and finishing their degrees.
He said the government had taken steps to publish SSC and HSC results within 60 days and expedite re-evaluation results, which are scheduled to be published on November 23.
Milon said DU had been asked to complete its admission process quickly, but its own plans eventually led him to refer the matter to the court.
He also questioned the tendency among teachers to approach the High Court over various issues, saying problems should first be addressed through discussion and coordination.
The minister said universities should not open new departments without considering labour market demands. Instead, academic programmes should equip graduates with skills relevant to the workplace.
Highlighting staff shortages from primary schools to universities, he called for a prompt assessment of manpower requirements and criticised delays in decision-making between universities and the UGC.
On DU's autonomy, Milon said the university could claim its autonomous status under the 1974 Act but should also coordinate with the government when necessary.
He questioned the university's expectation of government funding while asserting its autonomy, saying coordination was essential.
The minister urged DU to develop effective plans to eliminate session jams, strengthen research and generate employment.

item.title: COP31 talks enter overtime as latest draft omits fossil fuel phase-out
item.description:
Negotiations at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya have extended beyond the scheduled deadline, with the latest draft of the proposed outcome facing criticism for failing to include an explicit commitment to transition away from fossil fuels.
The draft, released early Sunday, retains a target for electricity to account for 35% of global energy consumption by 2035 and introduces a goal of scaling up carbon capture to gigaton levels by the same year.
However, it makes no direct reference to fossil fuels, offers no concrete roadmap for phasing them out and weakens several provisions that countries and campaigners had hoped would translate previous climate pledges into action.
The omission has renewed concerns about the ambition of the negotiations, particularly as developing countries continue to demand stronger commitments on climate finance, adaptation and support for communities facing the impacts of global warming.
David Waskow, international climate director at the World Resources Institute, described the draft as a limited step forward.
"It's a package to move us forward in limited ways, but leaves a lot of work to do," he said.
"There is no new language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, and that is a missed opportunity for sure."
The latest draft, like its predecessor, does not explicitly mention fossil fuels. Instead, it recalls the UAE Consensus in its entirety, referring to the agreement reached at COP28 in Dubai in 2023.
The COP28 outcome called for a "just, orderly and equitable" transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems, alongside efforts to accelerate action during this critical decade.
While retaining that agreement provides continuity with previous climate commitments, the latest draft does not establish additional measures to implement the pledge.
It also excludes references to a Brazil-led roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels, which was expected to build on the Dubai agreement and provide a clearer pathway for implementation.
Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at 350.org, criticized the omission.
"They found room for a 2035 carbon capture target, yet struck the transition away from fossil fuels from the text and launched no initiative to take it forward," he said.
He blamed the Turkish and Australian presidencies for what he described as a failure of leadership.
One of the significant provisions retained in the draft is the target of increasing electricity's share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035.
The proposal had faced opposition from Saudi Arabia and several other countries during negotiations, partly because of concerns that electrification without a clear clean-energy requirement could encourage continued dependence on fossil fuel-based electricity generation.
The revised wording encourages countries to maximize the use of clean energy when expanding electrification.
However, it stops short of making clean electricity a binding requirement and recognizes that countries may pursue different pathways depending on their national circumstances.
Waskow said electrification was closely linked to reducing fossil fuel dependence across major sectors.
"That is really about moving away from fossil fuels in our cars, homes and factories," he said.
"Electrification is two sides of the same coin. It's about getting off fossil fuels."
The draft acknowledges that global warming is expected to exceed the 1.5C threshold above pre-industrial levels in the coming years.
It calls on countries to limit both the extent and duration of this overshoot, reflecting growing scientific concerns about the consequences of temporarily exceeding the internationally agreed temperature limit.
The issue is expected to receive further attention at COP32 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, next year, where countries are scheduled to discuss the science of climate overshoot.
Exceeding 1.5C would increase the risks of extreme heat, floods, droughts and other climate-related disasters, placing additional pressure on vulnerable countries and communities.
For countries such as Bangladesh, which face significant exposure to climate-related hazards despite contributing relatively little to global emissions, limiting the extent of warming remains a critical priority.
The draft retains an ambition to scale up carbon capture to gigaton levels by 2035, although it removes the specific numerical targets included in Thursday's version.
It also states that carbon dioxide removal should "complement, and not substitute or delay" deep emissions reductions.
Carbon capture technologies are designed to trap carbon dioxide from industrial facilities and power plants before it enters the atmosphere, with the captured gas subsequently stored underground or used in industrial processes.
Supporters argue that the technology could help reduce emissions from hard-to-abate industries, particularly cement and steel production.
However, environmental campaigners question its effectiveness, high costs and potential to prolong dependence on fossil fuel infrastructure.
Jasper Inventor, head of the Greenpeace COP31 delegation, strongly criticized the latest draft.
"No deal is better than a deal with the fossil fuel industry, and if this is the final COP31 outcome then it is fundamentally unacceptable," he said.
He argued that the draft had weakened climate ambition while giving greater prominence to carbon capture technologies.
Beyond fossil fuels, several other important areas of the draft have also drawn attention.
On adaptation, the text retains a call to at least triple financial support to help countries respond to climate impacts by 2035.
It also proposes an "Antalya-Addis Ababa Roadmap" on adaptation finance, with a report expected at COP32. However, the draft does not specify a concrete financial target in dollar terms.
The proposed outcome also removes figures highlighting the gap between requested and delivered loss and damage funding, reducing the visibility of the financial shortfall facing vulnerable countries.
On renewable energy, the draft supports accelerating the expansion of clean energy but no longer repeats the COP28 commitment to triple global renewable energy capacity by 2030.
The proposed just transition provisions have also been weakened. The text refers only to "just transition pathways", while work on establishing a dedicated just transition mechanism has been pushed to next year.
The mechanism was expected to build on the agreement reached at COP30 in Brazil, which called for developing arrangements to support workers and communities affected by the transition away from fossil fuels.
Other provisions include a multi-year ocean initiative, known as the "Antalya Ocean Current", and plans for an ocean report to contribute to the next global stocktake of climate progress in 2028.
The draft also encourages the use of technologies to reduce methane emissions without setting a specific target.
In the Paris Agreement, it states that the accord is working, noting that projected global warming has declined from more than 4C to around 2.6C under current national climate plans. However, this remains significantly above the 1.5C threshold.
The final negotiations were scheduled to begin on Sunday morning, with discussions expected to continue through the afternoon as countries seek agreement on the remaining contentious issues.
Under the United Nations (UN) climate negotiation process, countries must reach consensus before the final decision can be adopted.
Governments can raise objections, request amendments or withhold agreement if they consider the proposed language unacceptable.
With disagreements persisting over fossil fuel transition, adaptation finance and just transition arrangements, the final outcome will test whether COP31 can deliver meaningful progress beyond the commitments already made at previous climate summits.

item.title: 2 Dhaka College students sent to jail over campus crude bomb blast
item.description:
Two Dhaka College students have been sent to jail, while a third, who is a minor, has been sent to a juvenile development centre in connection with a crude bomb explosion on the college campus.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jamshed Alam passed the order on Sunday following an application by the investigation officer.
Sirajam Munira, judge of Dhaka Children's Court-2, sent the minor to the Tongi Juvenile Development Centre in Gazipur.
SI Moktar Hossain of the prosecution department confirmed the matter.
The three students were detained from two dormitories of Dhaka College around midnight on Saturday over allegations of involvement in the explosion. Later, the college’s chief assistant, Md Abu Zayed, filed a case under the Explosives Act, 1884, with New Market police station.
The court subsequently produced the three accused. The investigation officer, SI Muhammad Sarwar Jahan Mehedi of New Market police station, sought to have the two adults sent to jail and the minor placed in a juvenile development centre.
There were no bail petitions on behalf of any of the accused, SI Moktar Hossain said.
According to the case statement, a loud explosion occurred at around 12:05am on Saturday between Bijoy-24 Hall and North Hall inside the college campus.
Students came out of their dormitories and went to the scene. Later, other students detained the three accused and, amid tension, assaulted them before taking them to the administrative building.
On receiving information, police from New Market police station took the three into custody from the students and took them to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for preliminary treatment.
The case alleges that three to four unidentified accomplices, acting in collusion with the accused, detonated a crude bomb-like explosive device to create panic among students, disrupt peace on campus and cause damage to lives and hall property.

item.title: Walton provides up to 30% discount on inverter ACs in Smart Exchange Offer
item.description:
Walton is offering up to 30% cash discount on its environment friendly and energy-efficient inverter air conditioners under its nationwide “AC Smart Exchange Offer.”
Customers can trade in an old AC of any brand to buy a Walton split, cassette or ceiling-type inverter model for residential or commercial use.
The offer took effect on November 3, 2026, and will remain available until further notice, the company said at an “AC Exchange Carnival” held recently at Walton’s corporate office in Dhaka.
Eva Rizwana Nilu, additional managing director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC, and Brigadier General (retd) Sajjad Hossain, deputy managing director, attended the event.
Tanvir Anjum, senior executive director, Zoheb Ahmed, chief marketing officer, and Firoj Alam, head of distributor network, were also present, among others.
Customers can bring their old split, cassette or ceiling-type ACs to Walton Plaza outlets or distributor showrooms nationwide.
The offer covers inverter split ACs with capacities ranging from 0.75 to 2.5 tonnes and inverter cassette and ceiling-type ACs ranging from 1.5 to 5 tonnes.
Md Tanvir Rahman, chief business officer of Walton AC, said the company had completely phased out the use of ozone-depleting CFC and HCFC refrigerants in its air conditioners, working with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, the Department of Environment and the United Nations Development Program.
He said Walton was the first company in Bangladesh to manufacture and market air conditioners using environment friendly R-290 and R-32 refrigerants. The company has run AC exchange campaigns since 2019 to help take older units containing CFCs and HCFCs out of use, he added.
Through the campaign, customers can replace ageing or non-functional ACs with energy-efficient inverter models that use either R-32 or R-290 refrigerant.
Rahman said the switch can help households and businesses lower electricity bills and reduce emissions associated with electricity use.
Walton manufactures and markets a range of smart inverter split ACs, including its Super Saver models, which have received the highest energy rating from the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI).
It also manufactures inverter cassette and ceiling-type ACs, variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems and chillers for medium-sized and large premises.
Walton ACs come with a one-year replacement facility and a compressor guarantee of up to 12 years.

item.title: Southeast Bank awards 66 children of employees for outstanding academic achievements
item.description:
Southeast Bank PLC has honoured 66 meritorious children of its employees for their outstanding academic achievements in 2026.
These students secured GPA-5 in the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination and obtained A Grades in at least six subjects in the O-Level examinations.
The event was presided over by Md Khalid Mahmood Khan, managing director of Southeast Bank PLC.
The event was graced by MA Kashem, chairman of Southeast Bank PLC, as chief guest.
He handed over crests, certificates and gift items to the meritorious students in recognition of their hard work and dedication.
He commended the students for their hard work, dedication and perseverance, while also acknowledging the invaluable support and encouragement of their families.
MA Kashem, chairman of Southeast Bank PLC, said: “Today’s meritorious students are the leaders of tomorrow. They should always remember that ‘Sky is the Limit’—there is no limit to dreaming big and achieving success. With confidence, hard work, integrity and perseverance, they can reach the highest heights in life. May today's achievements serve as a stepping stone towards even greater success in the future. Their accomplishments are not merely individual achievements; they reflect the collective efforts of their families, society and institutions. Southeast Bank takes great pride in recognizing merit, talent and excellence and remains committed to nurturing and encouraging the potential of the younger generation.”
The event was also attended by special guests Rehana Rahman, vice chairperson of Southeast Bank PLC.; Aziz AI Kaiser, chairman of board of trustees, North South University, Benajir Ahmed, member of the board of trustees of North South University, and Prof Abdul Hannan Chowdhury, vice chancellor of North South University.
Other senior executives of the bank were also present at the event.
The award ceremony reflects Southeast Bank PLC.'s commitment to the overall wellbeing of its employees and their families, while reaffirming the Bank's long-standing commitment to education and social responsibility.

item.title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank platinum sponsor of Blue Star Team in BCB’s ‘D-3 Trophy’
item.description:
Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC has signed a Platinum Sponsorship Agreement with Blue Star, one of the participating teams in the ‘Domestic Three (D-3) Trophy’, a domestic cricket tournament organized by the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB).
The agreement was signed on Sunday, November 22, at the bank’s head office.
At the signing ceremony, managing director of Al-Arafah Islami Bank Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan handed over the agreement to the Blue Star team captain Nurul Hasan Sohan.
The ceremony was attended by deputy managing directors of Al-Arafah Islami Bank Mohammed Fazlur Rahman Chowdhury and Sayed Abul Hashem, along with Shanian Taneem, owner of Blue Star, cricketer Enamul Haque Bijoy, and other senior officials from both organizations.
BCB’s ‘D-3 Trophy’ is a new tournament aimed at making domestic cricket in the country more competitive and attractive.
Featuring six franchise-based teams competing across three formats, Blue Star is one of the participating teams.
Alongside providing financial services, Al-Arafah Islami Bank continues to contribute to the overall development of the country through its support for education, sports, and various social welfare initiatives.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Hasina must return under prisoner exchange deal
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has said that Sheikh Hasina, who is currently staying in India, must be brought back to Bangladesh under the existing prisoner exchange agreement between the two countries.
She expressed hope that India would honour the legal process and hand Hasina over to Bangladesh.
She made the remarks while addressing a rally as the chief guest at Joy Bangla intersection in Nagarkanda upazila of Faridpur on Sunday evening. The rally was organised by Jubo Dal to protest terrorism and anarchy across the country.
“If Sheikh Hasina is to return to the country, it must be through the prisoner exchange agreement. We hope India will comply with this and hand her over to Bangladesh,” Shama Obaed said.
The state minister also made it clear what would happen to Hasina after her return, saying she would be sent to the Central Jail.
She said Hasina would not be brought back through routine paperwork or a passport but through the existing legal framework and prisoner exchange agreement between the two countries to face trial.
“Have we forgotten how our former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia was left to suffer without medical treatment? Have we forgotten how our current prime minister was tortured and forced to leave the country?” she asked.
Warning party activists against sheltering Awami League members, Shama Obaed said: “If I find that an Awami League associate is hiding in the house of any Zia's soldier in my constituency, that Zia's soldier will also be in trouble. However, there is nothing wrong with being an ordinary Awami League supporter. Anyone has the right to support a political party.”
Urging party leaders and activists to remain united, she warned that internal conflicts and factionalism would give fascist forces an opportunity to regroup.
“No ordinary citizen, whether a BNP, Awami League or other political party supporter, should face retaliatory treatment anywhere in the country, from Teknaf to Tetulia. We do not want that,” she added.
The rally was chaired by Nagarkanda upazila Jubo Dal President Taibur Rahman Masud.
Faridpur district BNP Convener Syed Modarres Ali Isha, Joint Conveners Syed Zulfikar Hossain Jewel and Khandaker Fazlul Haque Tulu, among others, addressed the gathering.

item.title: BRAC University launches Fahim Saleh scholarship, entrepreneurship fund
item.description:
BRAC University has established the Fahim Saleh Scholarship and the Fahim Saleh Youth Entrepreneurship Endowment Fund with a donation from the parents of the late Fahim Saleh, co-founder of ride-sharing platform Pathao.
The initiatives were announced at a ceremony on the university's Merul Badda campus in Dhaka on Sunday, November 22, 2026.
Fahim, a Bangladeshi-American entrepreneur, co-founded Pathao in 2015 and Gokada in 2018. He also supported entrepreneurs in emerging markets through Adventure Capital and Launch Africa Ventures.
He believed businesses addressing local challenges could grow beyond their markets and that young Bangladeshis had the potential to build successful ventures.
At the ceremony, his father, Saleh Uddin Ahmed, signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with BRAC University Treasurer Ariful Islam regarding the donation.
Speaking about the initiative, Islam said the university considered it a privilege to help carry forward Fahim's legacy.
He thanked BRAC Institute of Languages Founder and Adviser Lady Syeda Sarwat Abed and former United Nations official Humayun Kabir for facilitating the connection with the donor family.
BRAC University Vice-Chancellor Professor Syed Ferhat Anwar said the endowment should be treated as a cause rather than merely a financial contribution.
He suggested that the entrepreneurship award could encourage young innovators to develop practical solutions to societal challenges, including road safety. He also announced that the university would match the donation.
At the event, second-semester law student Jannatul Ferdous Sifat spoke about how the university's need-based scholarship had helped her continue her education while her parents were undergoing medical treatment and her family depended on her elder sister's income.
"I refuse to let my circumstances define my horizon," she said, describing the scholarship as an opportunity to move "from survival to growth".
Soumik Hasan Shranto, co-founder and head of marketing at underwater autonomous systems company Dubotech Digital Ltd, also spoke about how BRAC University's Centre for Entrepreneurship Development (CED) had supported his startup.
Saleh Uddin Ahmed thanked the university authorities for honouring his son's memory through the initiatives.
The ceremony was moderated by Khairul Basher, director of the university's Office of Communications.
Among others, Afshana Choudhury, head of CED; Registrar Dave Dowland; and Saiduzzaman Shikder, head of the International and Scholarship Office, attended the event.
The initiatives are aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

item.title: RMG stakeholders call for permanent wage-setting framework
item.description:
Representatives of Bangladesh’s garment industry, labour organizations and the Minimum Wage Board have called for a permanent, transparent and evidence-based framework for determining workers’ wages while ensuring the industry’s sustainability and competitiveness.
The call came at a virtual dialogue titled “Garment Workers’ Wages: Fairness and Industry Development”, organized by the Power and Participation Research Centre (PPRC) under its Ajker Agenda series on Sunday.
Hosted by PPRC Executive Chairman Hossain Zillur Rahman, the discussion brought together industry leaders, labour representatives and a member of the Minimum Wage Board ahead of its scheduled meeting on November 23.
Opening the discussion, Hossain Zillur Rahman identified 3 priorities: fair wages, sustainable industrial growth and an orderly institutional process for wage determination. He said inadequate preparation and the absence of a clearly defined framework had repeatedly made wage negotiations contentious.
On the basis for revising wages, he noted that the Tk12,500 entry-level wage introduced in November 2023 had subsequently received annual increments of 5% and 9% on basic pay, alongside corresponding house rent adjustments. These changes brought the earlier wage structure to approximately Tk15,044 in 2026, he calculated, adding that the adjustment largely reflected inflation rather than real wage growth.
Syed Sultan Uddin Ahmed, executive director of the Bangladesh Institute of Labour Studies (BILS), said the absence of a national minimum wage and clearly defined criteria remained major institutional weaknesses.
He called for workers’ actual living costs, supported by data from PPRC’s State of the Real Economy survey and the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics, to form the basis of wage decisions. He also urged the Minimum Wage Board to prepare its own research-based proposal instead of beginning negotiations with competing demands from workers and employers.
“The Minimum Wage Board should have its own research report. It should examine the available evidence and prepare a proposal, instead of starting with two widely divergent demands,” he said.
Mahmud Hasan Khan, president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), acknowledged the need for fair wages but highlighted the pressures facing manufacturers. He said 287 factories had closed over the previous 3 years, while 669 factories had been affected by recent unrest, with disruptions lasting between 1 and 21 days.
He said inflation, productivity, previous wage adjustments, infrastructure constraints and international competitiveness should be considered in determining wages. He added that a worker could earn approximately Tk19,520 a month, including 78 hours of overtime, attendance bonuses and other incentives.
Mahmud also said BGMEA had engaged with 82 registered and unregistered labour federations to encourage dialogue. He called for clear guidelines governing future annual wage adjustments.
Taslima Akhter, president of Bangladesh Garment Sromik Samhati, argued that minimum wages should be based on a normal 8-hour working day rather than earnings dependent on overtime. She cited workers’ proposals of Tk30,000 for apprentices and Tk32,000 for Grade 4 workers.
She said a dignified wage should cover nutritious food, suitable housing, children's education and healthcare. Welcoming the reduction of the wage revision interval from 5 years to 3 years, she also called for stronger workers’ rights and freedom of association.
Anwarul Alam Parvez, president of the Bangladesh Chamber of Industries (BCI), highlighted stagnant export earnings, rising financing costs, inadequate infrastructure and declining competitiveness. He said export earnings had remained broadly within $36-39 billion over recent financial years.
He called for industrial diversification, skills development, technical education and higher-value manufacturing to strengthen the industry's capacity to support higher wages.
Meanwhile, Musleh Uddin Ahmed, independent member of the Minimum Wage Board and professor of public administration at the University of Dhaka, said Board members had visited factories in Chattogram and Narayanganj to consult workers and employers. He also referred to government commitments to establish healthcare facilities in 6 labor-intensive areas.
In his concluding remarks, Hossain Zillur Rahman said wage policy should go beyond minimum and take-home earnings to address workers’ broader living conditions, including housing, healthcare, education and transportation.
He identified a shared recognition among participants of the need for systematic wage determination and a permanent institutional framework to make future revisions more predictable.

item.title: Crude bomb blasts in Malibagh, near Kabi Nazrul College injure 3
item.description:
Two crude bomb explosions rocked Malibagh and the area outside Kabi Nazrul Government College on Sunday, leaving three people injured.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Shahjahanpur Police station Amirul Islam said two crude bombs exploded inside the government officers’ residential quarters adjacent to Abuzar Giffari College in Malibagh, including one on the college playground.
No casualties were reported in the Malibagh incidents. Police are analysing CCTV footage to identify those responsible, he added.
Meanwhile, two crude bombs exploded in front of Kabi Nazrul Government College in the afternoon, injuring a college employee and two students.
Confirming the incident, Sutrapur Police Station OC Matiur Rahman said the authorities would take action against those involved.

item.title: Brilliant Verstappen wins Las Vegas Grand Prix
item.description:
Red Bull driver Max Verstappen roared to a superb victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday, holding his nerve in a thrilling 50-lap battle to claim the 75th win of his career.
Verstappen dug deep to fend off Mercedes' newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli and teammate George Russell in a race that saw a jaw-dropping 35 lead changes.
McLaren's Lando Norris took second place while Oscar Piastri finished third at the end of a hectic final few laps which saw Russell strike a wall before Antonelli faded down the stretch.
"Crazy, I mean really, really surreal -- something that I've never seen before in Formula One myself," Verstappen said after clinching victory by six tenths of a second.
"Just a crazy amount of fighting. The slipstream was so big that it was just impossible to drive off. Crazy how many people were just following.
"So yeah, very happy with such a crazy race to come out on top."
Verstappen's victory leaves the Dutchman second in the standings with 304 points, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton third on 267 points. Russell is fourth with 264 points, the same total as Norris.
With the drivers' championship already settled, Verstappen started on pole looking for a win to boost his chances of finishing second behind Antonelli.
The pre-race build-up had been dominated by talk of tension between Verstappen and Mercedes' driver Russell, who had been irked by the Dutch driver during Friday's final practice.
Russell had angrily declared that "somebody has got to stand up to that guy", and for long periods of Saturday's thriller the 28-year-old British driver seemed determined to take on the challenge.
Russell swarmed all over his rival, with the duo swapping first and second throughout a chaotic race but Verstappen always looked to have the Briton's measure.
Eventually it was Antonelli who emerged as Verstappen's biggest threat, the Italian passing Russell to take second on lap 39 and then scrapping relentlessly with Verstappen for the remainder of the race.
Russell's challenge came to an abrupt end on lap 48 as he locked up and clipped a wall. Antonelli then suffered a loss of power that allowed Norris and Piastri to force their way onto the podium.
"I think that must have been the most chaotic race ever in the history of Formula One," Norris said afterwards.
"I didn't know what was happening half the time. It had everything. It was tough. A fun day. Chaotic. But a fun day."
Teammate Piastri added: "They say Las Vegas is the entertainment capital of the world and I think that was pretty entertaining.
"Every time you caught the back of the train or you overtook someone you thought you were going to win the race by 10 seconds, but then you'd get ahead and suddenly realize that the slipstream was doing a lot of help," the Australian added.
"A crazy race to be part of but very happy to end it on the podium."
There was drama behind the leaders, with Ferrari duo Hamilton and Charles Leclerc locking horns -- and cars -- once again after their tussle at the Mexican Grand Prix.
Hamilton and Leclerc collided as they battled on lap 38. Hamilton eventually finished in seventh place, with Leclerc crossing in 10th.
It marked another stormy episode between the two Ferrari drivers, with Hamilton at one stage urging the pit team to tell Leclerc to "back off" as he attempted to chase the leading pack.
Leclerc and Hamilton had also clashed at the Mexican Grand Prix on the opening lap, wrecking the team's hopes of victory.

item.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev for ATP Finals title
item.description:
Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time.
The world number three showed signs of vulnerability but fought through to beat the American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/1).
He will play Zverev in Sunday's decider, after the two-time Finals champion beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7/0), 6-4 in the other last-four match-up.
"It's going to be a high-level match," Zverev said.
"We had a practice before the tournament started, it was unbelievable, we played one set for one-and-a-half hours so I hope it's going to be similar tomorrow.
"I hope both of us are going to be at our best and hopefully it's going to be an entertaining match for everybody."
Alcaraz lost to Italian Jannik Sinner in the season-ender's showpiece match last year and will aim to go one better this time around in Turin.
He has been dealing with a left-thigh injury since Wednesday but, playing with his leg heavily strapped, he extended his winning streak to 13 matches, a run that includes title-winning campaigns in Vienna and Paris.
However, it was a hard-fought victory as the Spaniard struggled to play with his usual freedom before pulling through in just over two hours.
"I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning," said the seven-time Grand Slam winner.
"But I'm just happy that I came back in the second set... and ended up playing good tennis."
- 'Excited for tomorrow' -
Having dropped only 15 games across his three round-robin matches without once losing his own serve, Alcaraz was broken in his very first service game against Shelton.
The 23-year-old quickly fell behind 3-0 and was unable to claw his way back into the set.
In the second frame, Alcaraz upped his level, gaining the upper hand by breaking to lead 5-3 before levelling at one set all.
The deciding set remained tight, with neither player facing a break point, forcing the match into a tie-break.
Shelton faltered with two unforced errors allowing the Spaniard to pull ahead 5-1, a deficit from which the American could not recover.
"I think the third set was even closer. I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set, myself as well," said Alcaraz.
"Great points, great games, and just happy to play great tennis in the tie-breaker... I'm excited for tomorrow."
Earlier in the month, Alcaraz beat Shelton in the Paris Masters final to win the title for the first time -- a measure of revenge on the American who had ended his US Open title defence in September.
Alcaraz, who missed a chunk of the season with a wrist issue, will nonetheless be able to end his year on a high if he can next beat the man who took his French Open title during his injury-enforced absence.
In claiming that title in Paris, as well as the US Open crown, Zverev catapulted himself above Alcaraz and Sinner in the rankings to world No. 1.
In a repeat of the 2021 Finals title match, which the 29-year-old German also won, Zverev saw off Russian Medvedev in straight sets.
A tightly-contested first frame rattled to a tie-break, which the two-time major winner raced through as Medvedev crumbled, failing to win a point.
The first break points of the match came in the seventh game of the second set, with Medvedev double-faulting to hand Zverev the advantage.
The big-serving Hamburg native, who is yet to drop a set, then served out the match to set up a final meeting between the tournament's top two seeds.
The last meeting between Zverev and Alcaraz came in the semi-finals of the Australian Open in January, with the Spaniard winning in five sets en route to completing his career Grand Slam.

item.title: Class 1 admission: Apply on Dec 1, digital lottery Dec 15
item.description:
The applications for admission into Class 1 for the 2027 academic year in all private schools and colleges across the country will commence on December 1.
The application window will remain open until December 10. Students for Class 1 will be selected via online digital lottery at 11 am on December 15.
The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) issued directives regarding this on November 19. The guidelines signed by the Director (Secondary) of the Directorate, detailed the admission process across secondary, lower secondary and attached primary levels in private schools and colleges nationwide including those in Dhaka city.
According to the directives, applications for Class 1 admission will be accepted exclusively online at http://gsa.teletalk.com.bd. The application fee is set at Taka 110 which must be paid via SMS using a Teletalk prepaid mobile connection.
Applicants may select up to five schools in order of preference, subject to availability. If an applicant chooses both shifts of an institution that operates on a double-shift basis, each shift will count as one of the five choices. It will not be possible to select the same school or shift more than once.
Meanwhile, admissions for classes 2 through 9 must be conducted through written examinations, managed by the respective institution's own admission committee.
In this process, the 2027 admission policy for private schools and colleges must be followed. Furthermore, instructions have been provided to ensure adherence to various quotas and catchment area requirements.
The directives also stated that the heads of institutions must publish an admission notice specifying the number of vacant seats available at their institutions. The notice must clearly state the date and time for the submission of application forms.
The DSHE has confirmed that the selection of students for Class 1 will be conducted through an online digital lottery. The admission process must be conducted under the constant guidance and supervision of the Admission Oversight and Monitoring Committee.
At the same time, transparency and accountability must be ensured throughout the entire admission process.
Detailed guidelines regarding the completion of admission applications and other admission-related procedures can be found in the 'Secondary Circular/Order' section of the DSHE website (www.dshe.gov.bd), as well as on the Teletalk website (www.teletalk.com.bd). All relevant educational institutions have been instructed to carry out the admission process in accordance with the admission policy prescribed by the Ministry of Education.

item.title: National Robotics Championship 2026 draws over 280 teams at IUBAT
item.description:
The National Robotics Championship (NRC) 2026 was held at the International University of Business Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT) campus in Uttara, Dhaka, bringing together more than 280 teams from across the country.
The national-level competition aimed to promote scientific thinking, innovation, technological skills and creativity among young people, while encouraging them to apply science and technology to real-world challenges.
Organised by IUBAT in collaboration with its Innovation and Entrepreneurship Centre (IIEC) and the National Robotics Championship, the event provided a platform for students to showcase their robotics projects, engineering skills and problem-solving abilities.
IUBAT Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Abdur Rab chaired the programme, while renowned academic Professor Dr Mohammad Kaykobad attended as the chief guest.
The special guests included IUBAT Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Mahmudur Rahman; Professor Dr Dewan Muhammad Nuruzzaman, dean of the College of Engineering and chair of the Department of Mechanical Engineering; Professor Dr Sajal Saha, director of the Miyan Research Institute; and Dr Nayeem Hossain, director of IIEC.
Teams representing educational institutions from different parts of the country took part in the competition, demonstrating their technical knowledge, creativity, teamwork and practical engineering skills.
IUBAT said initiatives such as the championship aim to strengthen students' interest in science, technology, engineering and innovation, while preparing young people to meet the challenges of the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
The university also highlighted the importance of practical learning and research in developing future technology leaders and strengthening Bangladesh's position in an increasingly technology-driven world.

item.title: The new economics of staying cool
item.description:
For households in Bangladesh, keeping cool during the summer is increasingly becoming a balancing act between comfort and electricity costs. With rising power tariffs and concerns over global fuel supplies, families are paying closer attention to how much electricity their everyday appliances consume.
In June 2026, the average retail electricity tariff increased by 16.68%, rising from Tk 9.11 to Tk 10.63 per kilowatt-hour. The increase has added to the pressure on household budgets, making energy management an increasingly important consideration.
While factories and businesses are exploring alternative energy sources to reduce their dependence on grid electricity, such options remain less practical for most households. Families still rely on conventional power to operate essential appliances such as refrigerators, televisions and air conditioners.
Among these, air conditioners can account for a substantial share of household electricity consumption. Yet, in Bangladesh's hot and humid climate, cutting back on cooling is not always a realistic option. The challenge, therefore, is not simply to use less electricity but to understand where it goes and how consumption can be managed.
One of the biggest difficulties with traditional household electricity use is the lack of visibility. Consumers often discover how much power they have used only after receiving their monthly bills. By that point, the opportunity to adjust their consumption during the billing period has already passed.
Smart appliances with real-time monitoring features offer a different approach. Rather than relying entirely on monthly bills, users can track electricity consumption as it happens and make adjustments to their daily routines.
This can be particularly useful for air conditioners, whose energy consumption varies depending on room temperature, operating hours and cooling settings. Monitoring these factors can help households identify usage patterns and make more informed decisions about when and how to operate their appliances.
Some modern air conditioners also offer smartphone connectivity, allowing users to adjust settings remotely. Such features add convenience while giving consumers greater control over their cooling habits.
Newer models are increasingly combining automated cooling with energy-monitoring tools. Haier’s Gravity AI Series, for example, features AI Climate Master, which adjusts cooling settings according to room conditions, alongside AI ECO for energy management and AI Electricity Monitoring, which allows users to track power consumption.
Together, these features aim to reduce the need for constant manual adjustments while helping households better understand their energy consumption.
However, smart technology alone cannot guarantee lower electricity bills. Actual costs depend on several factors, including appliance efficiency, room conditions, operating hours and individual usage patterns. Monitoring consumption is therefore only the first step; making informed adjustments remains equally important.
As electricity prices and energy supply concerns continue to shape household spending, the focus is gradually shifting from simply paying monthly bills to understanding everyday consumption. For families unwilling to compromise on indoor comfort, smarter appliances and accessible energy-monitoring tools could offer a more practical way to manage the cost of staying cool.

item.title: The ‘sad’ new economics of smartphones
item.description:
For nearly a decade, the smartphone market followed a predictable trajectory: every year brought faster processors, sharper screens, and larger batteries at roughly the same price points.
Over the past 18 months, however, that formula has inverted. From entry-level handsets to flagships, retail tags have climbed noticeably across global markets—and in Bangladesh, consumers are feeling a compounded squeeze.
Rather than a temporary pricing anomaly, industry data indicates that the smartphone sector is undergoing a structural cost reset.
Understanding why devices have become costlier—and why relief is unlikely in 2027—requires looking at the semiconductor supply chain, changing manufacturer economics, and local fiscal policies.
Core drivers behind the global price surge
The primary catalyst behind rising handset prices is not camera hardware or display technology, but an acute global memory crunch triggered by the artificial intelligence boom.
Why Chinese OEMs can no longer rescue budget buyers
Historically, whenever smartphone prices crept upward, Chinese original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) like Xiaomi, Realme, Vivo, Oppo, and Transsion (Tecno, Infinix, Itel) stepped in to undercut competitors with aggressive spec-to-price ratios.
In the current cycle, that buffer has largely disappeared.
Chinese brands traditionally operated on razor-thin hardware margins of 3% to 5% in the sub-$200 bracket, relying on massive shipment volumes and software ecosystem monetization to stay profitable.
When memory and chipset costs spike by 20% or more, a 5% margin leaves zero room to absorb the shock.
Unlike Apple or Samsung, which command higher profit margins and stronger bulk-purchasing leverage, budget-focused Android vendors face a stark choice: raise retail prices or exit ultra-low-cost tiers altogether.
Indeed, several major Chinese manufacturers raised retail prices across their 2026 lineups, while brands like Oppo scaled back ultra-budget sub-$100 shipments to avoid selling hardware at a loss.
Global and South Asian market trends
Comparing today's market to the pre-2024 landscape highlights how sharply consumer dynamics have shifted.
Prior to 2024—and particularly during the 2020–2023 cycle—smartphones were abundant and comparatively inexpensive, driven by fierce competition in 4G handsets and falling component costs.
Even in 2024, global smartphone shipments rebounded by 6.4% as emerging markets snapped up affordable Android devices.
By contrast, 2025 and 2026 mark a clear contraction in unit volume alongside rising market value:
Metric / Segment
Pre-2024 / 2024 Baseline
2025–2026 Reality
Global Shipments
Steady recovery (+6.4% YoY in 2024)
Projected 16.7% YoY drop in 2026; Q3 2026 hit a 14-year quarterly low
Sub-$100 Entry Tier
Core growth engine in South Asia
Collapsed by ~91% YoY in India in Q3 2026 (shrinking to under 2% market share)
Mid-Premium ($400–$600)
Niche upgrade tier (4% share in India)
Fastest-growing segment (+79.8% YoY in India in Q3 2026), fueled by EMI financing
Replacement Cycle
~2.5 to 3 years
Extending past 3.5–4 years as buyers hold devices longer
Across South Asia, India's smartphone market remained flat at 152 million units in 2025 before contracting 23.3% year-over-year in Q3 2026—its weakest festive quarter in a decade.
While unit volumes fell, buyers increasingly relied on zero-interest Equated Monthly Installments (EMI) and trade-in programs to purchase durable mid-range and premium devices rather than replacing cheap phones every two years.
The Bangladesh squeeze: Taxes, NEIR, and local assembly
For Bangladeshi consumers, global supply-chain inflation collides with one of South Asia's steepest tax regimes.
Complete Built Unit (CBU) imported smartphones face a cumulative tax burden of roughly 57% to 64.25%—comprising a 25% customs duty, 15% VAT, 5% advance income tax, and supplementary duties.
Although the National Board of Revenue (NBR) temporarily trimmed customs duty to 10% in January 2026 (lowering the effective tax to ~43.4%), the concession expired on July 1, 2026, restoring the 64.25% tax wall and triggering immediate 20% to 25% price jumps on imported devices.
Historically, price-conscious buyers bypassed these taxes via the informal "grey" or luggage-party market, which previously captured over 40% of market value.
However, grey market sales have contracted significantly in 2026 following the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission's (BTRC) rollout of the National Equipment Identity Register (NEIR).
With unregistered IMEIs facing network restrictions and tighter airport baggage enforcement, consumers have become far more cautious about spending tens of thousands of Taka on unofficial handsets.
At the same time, locally assembled "Made in Bangladesh" smartphones—which supply the bulk of the country's entry and mid-tier demand—have not been immune to price hikes.
Local factories still import 100% of their core components (motherboards, displays, batteries, and memory chips) in US dollars.
Furthermore, tax incidence on local manufacturing has crept upward over the years to roughly 35% (compared to 12% duty and zero VAT when local assembly launched in 2017).
Caught between higher global RAM costs, Taka-to-Dollar exchange pressures, and local tax overhead, domestic assemblers were forced to raise retail prices by Tk500 to Tk5,000 across popular models in 2026.
Adapting to the new normal
While the era of ultra-cheap, high-spec smartphones has paused, the market is maturing in ways that benefit long-term ownership.
Manufacturers are compensating for higher hardware prices by extending OS and security update guarantees to four, five, or even seven years—meaning a mid-range device bought today remains secure and functional far longer than budget phones of the pre-2024 era.
Combined with wider availability of bank EMI plans and official trade-in schemes in Bangladesh, consumers are steadily shifting from frequent, low-cost upgrades to smarter, longer-lasting investments.

item.title: Shafiqur: Jamaat won’t join local polls if expats denied voting rights
item.description:
Leader of the Opposition and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr Shafiqur Rahman on Sunday said his party would not participate in the upcoming local government elections if expatriate Bangladeshis were denied the opportunity to vote.
“We are hearing that our expatriate brothers and sisters will be left out of the local government elections. We are making it clear again: if they are not given the opportunity this time, we will not be in the election either,” he said.
Shafiqur made the remarks at a discussion session titled “July Uprising and Aftermath | Voices from Australia” in Campbelltown, New South Wales, Australia.
He recalled that his party had taken a similar stand before the national election, telling the interim government and the Election Commission that it would not contest unless expatriates, whom he called remittance warriors, were enrolled as voters.
The opposition leader said expatriates were able to register as voters for the first time in their lives before the last general election.
He said expatriates continue to face disrespect at home, alleging mistreatment at airports and claiming that some had been physically assaulted. “This is a shame for the nation,” he said, adding that other countries welcome their diaspora with respect.
Shafiqur said he had come to Australia to advocate not for financial remittances but for “intellectual remittance”, urging Bangladeshi academics and professionals abroad to return and contribute to the country.
“If Allah gives us the opportunity, we will not treat you as guests. We will treat you as brothers, sons and fathers,” he said.
Referring to the issue of expatriates' rights, the Jamaat chief said Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman, a former lawmaker, had been arrested and sent to jail for protesting against their alleged deprivation, and was released a month later.
He also claimed that 54 Bangladeshis were still imprisoned in different countries for taking part in protests during the July 2024 mass uprising.
The opposition leader is on a weeklong visit to Australia and Malaysia from November 20 to 26.
